jsonld.description: See how your savings grow over time with regular deposits and compound interest, or find out how long it will take to reach a savings goal.

mainEntity.name: What interest rate should I use for a savings account?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use your actual account's APY if you know it — high-yield savings accounts and standard accounts can differ significantly in rate.

mainEntity.name: Does this account for taxes on interest earned?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if you choose a taxable account — enter your federal bracket and state rate and the calculator deducts tax on each year's interest. Choose Tax-Free / Roth to see gross growth.

mainEntity.name: Is a high-yield savings account safe?

acceptedAnswer.text: FDIC-insured high-yield accounts (up to standard insurance limits) carry the same safety as a traditional bank account — the higher rate typically reflects lower overhead costs for online-only banks, not higher risk.

mainEntity.name: How much should I keep in savings vs. invest?

acceptedAnswer.text: A common guideline is 3-6 months of expenses in accessible savings for emergencies, with additional long-term savings directed toward investment accounts for higher growth potential.

mainEntity.name: How big should my emergency fund be?

acceptedAnswer.text: A common guideline is 3-6 months of essential living expenses, though the right number depends on job stability, dependents, and other financial safety nets you may have.
